title: Research: native warp relations add no paired-extraction directions
body:
The six-skip construction treats 72 warp IDs as independent symbols, although they represent only 58 distinct native maps. This package proves that evaluating the actual native maps does **not** enlarge either rational scalar paired-extraction space on the fixed PR3042/3054 words. It is a **scoped negative result; no new κ**.

For both providers, the identity and 58 native operators are rationally independent, with all 512 columns and phases included. Merging duplicate maps removes 184 symbolic terms, but exact rational bases and modular rank certificates prove the right/left spaces remain 119/181-dimensional. Their scalar pairing is therefore unchanged for every terminal support, including simultaneous directions. The result does not rule out changed words, operator-valued interfaces, or cheaper synthesis of existing directions.

Validation: the registered Python 3.12 replay and nine behavioral test groups pass, including a case where aliasing really does enlarge a space, missing-constraint and rank-dropping-prime controls, phase/source failures, and a separate noncommuting vector interpreter. Optimized Python 3.12 and a Git-free Python 3.14 export reproduce the identical receipt. All 15 committed package files match the tested bytes. The checker imports no predecessor Python and needs only the standard library.

Reproduce: `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/native-warp-extraction-boundary`.
Expected: `PASS_NATIVE_WARP_EXTRACTION_BOUNDARY` and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, outcome `negative-result`.

Base: `997e6a9ca7b4f95d50e366f61412fd640d72a88a`. PR3042: `84cc406ad91ec53fff329a11a445d7effe564a77`; PR3054: `4773c3ea67b471415870e38411fae313ec44a675`. Refreshed main and reviewed new PR metadata through #3131; its dense collector work is separate. The selected frontier and upstream files are unchanged. Native/compiler, physical, precision, common-label, caller and analytic assumptions remain predecessor obligations; no complete supplier or outer replay is claimed here.

Credit Cinna Davis/PR2226, Jeremy Diviney/PR2908, Mason Hale/PR2917, Marius-Paul Dumitrean/PR2979, dcharb78/PR3042, Nick Petalas/PR3054, Jeremy Kothe, dataisfire/PR3115 and the retained geometry/native contributors. Tekalign, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no independent human or proof-kernel review claimed. Apache-2.0. Proof, source pins, limitations and open next questions are in the package README.
